newsitem.title: USA: White House said to miss subpoena deadline.
newsitem.headline: White House said to miss subpoena deadline.

text.p: A House committee investigating campaign fund-raising abuses said Monday that the White House had missed a noon deadline for delivering subpoenaed documents.

The Government Reform and Oversight Committee said the documents related to John Huang, a former Commerce Department and Democratic National Committee official; the Lippo Group, an Indonesian company, and the Riady family, contributors to the Democrats.

Committee Chairman Dan Burton, an Indiana Republican who presented two subpoenas relating to Huang and the Riadys to White House counsel James Ruff last Wednesday, said the committee was being "stonewalled."

Burton said he expected additional subpoenas to be issued this week, at least one of them seeking documents relating to former Justice Department officials Webster Hubbell, who was hired as consultant with Lippo and others before he pleaded guilty to fraud charges.

Meanwhile, Sen John Glenn of Ohio, the senior Democrat on the Senate Government Affairs Committee, which is also investigating campaign fund-raising abuses, said he was asking staff to prepare subpoenas to look into possible foreign contributions to the Republican Party.

In a letter to committee chairman Fred Thompson, a Tennessee Republican, Glenn said an article in the latest issue of Time magazine strongly suggested that foreign money from Taiwan and Hong Kong might have been used by a "thinly diguised arm" of the Republican Party for political activity in the 1994 and 1996 federal elections.
Glenn said he would forward the subpoenas to Thompson and asked him to approve them within 72 hours.
